name: Facet
text: Use a *centered radial graph* with nodes that pulse brighter and faster as new data arrives, scaled to data volume. This makes new information immediately visible and draws attention without overwhelming the view. The trade-off is that radial layouts can clutter with dense data, but the pulse scaling keeps focus on what matters most.

name: Pane
text: The radial graph risks teaching users to ignore pulses entirely—like a stock ticker that blinks so often it becomes white noise. A better alternative is a *single, high-contrast flash* at the center when new data arrives, paired with a small, persistent counter for volume. Settle it by testing both: measure how quickly users notice and act on new data in a controlled demo.
